medfit Model Syntax

Source: R/sem-syntax-help.R
medfit-syntax.Rd

The model syntax read by fit_sem() and by fit_mediation(engine = "native"). It is a lavaan-style core plus two extensions, each marked "medfit extension" below. One statement per line (or separated by ;).

Core statements

StatementMeaning
y ~ x1 + x2regression of y on x1 and x2
f =~ y1 + y2 + y3latent variable f measured by the indicators
y1 ~~ y2covariance; y1 ~~ y1 a variance
y ~ x + m + x:mproduct term: the observed variable x * m as a regressor (see Product terms)
y ~ a*xlabel the path a; equal labels are one parameter
y ~ 0.5*xfix the path at 0.5
y ~ start(0.3)*x, lower(0)*, upper(1)*starting value, lower and upper bound
a == b, a + b == 1, cp == a*bequality constraint on labels; may be nonlinear
a < b, a > 0inequality constraint; label < number is a bound
ab := a*bdefined parameter, with a delta-method standard error

Constraints may be nonlinear in the labels (cp == a*b, a*b == 0.1, a*b > 0.1, ab > 0 with ab := a*b), solved with the Jacobian recomputed at every point; a model with one tries every start and keeps the best accepted solution, warning when the starts disagree. A product of labels set to zero (a*b == 0, b1*b2*b3 == 0) is instead solved exactly: one linear fit per factor (a == 0, b == 0), keeping the smallest discrepancy. A sum of products (a1*b1 + a2*b2 == 0) has no exact reduction, so it is best-effort: the fit is the best of the starts tried, a disagreement warning means a better optimum may exist, and n_starts raises the number of starts. Labels used in a constraint or a definition must be defined in the model. A constraint with no free parameter is an error. Exogenous variables are given free variances and covariances, as lavaan does with fixed.x = FALSE; fixed_x = TRUE (or a vector of names) in fit_sem() fixes the moments of the selected ones at the sample values instead, as fixed.x = TRUE does. Unlike lavaan, which keeps an explicit x ~~ x or x ~ 1 free under fixed.x = TRUE and lets the degrees of freedom move, medfit stops with an error when the model has a statement on a selected variable's moments. Any intercept statement (y ~ 1, or 1 as a term: y ~ 1 + x) turns the mean structure on and frees every observed intercept the model does not write, as lavaan does; y ~ 0*1 then restricts the mean of y to 0 (one degree of freedom), and meanstructure = TRUE in fit_sem() turns it on without any statement, and a product term (x:m, see Product terms) always turns it on. A latent variable's mean is fixed at 0; a free latent ~1 is an error. A repeated 1 for one variable is an error. A variable cannot appear on both sides of ~ or =~ (y ~ y), and a path, a (co)variance or an intercept takes one row: a repeated y ~ x is an error, not a second row that competes for the label.

Product terms

x:m is the product of two observed variables, written with no spaces, on the right side of a regression (y ~ x + m + x:m). As in lavaan, the product is an observed exogenous variable: the engine builds the column x * m from data after listwise deletion, with a free variance, free covariances with the other exogenous variables and (the mean structure is on) a free mean. The likelihood does not change. x:m and m:x are one term, stored and printed under the canonical name, the two names sorted in the C locale (m:x); the coefficient is named y~m:x, or by its label (b*x:m labels the whole product). extract_mediation() finds the treatment-by-mediator product through the same name and returns the four-way decomposition; centering the mediator moves the split between the controlled direct effect and the reference interaction, not the natural effects.

A column in data named m:x or x:m is used only if it equals x * m on the rows kept; otherwise the fit stops. A product term turns the mean structure on, and meanstructure = FALSE is then an error. A coefficient equals the equation-wise least-squares estimate inside the class below, and the sandwich covariance (se_type = "sandwich") is the standard-error choice, because a product is not normal; the engine warns once when it is not used. fixed_x includes the product columns.

LimitMessage (starts with, or contains)
A space around :"a product ':' needs a variable name on each side, written without spaces (x:m)"
x:x"of a variable with itself is not supported"
x:m:w"a three-way or higher product"
Product as a left side (x:m ~ y, x:m ~~ y)"cannot be a left side"
Product in =~"is only valid on the right side of a regression"
Product inside a constraint or :="not inside the expression"
A latent variable in a product"products with latent variables are not supported in this version"
y ~ x:m + m:x (one product twice in an equation)"are the same product (canonical name"
A factor that is the target or downstream of it (y ~ x + x:y)"(rule 8: no outcome-derived regressors)"
A loop of regressions"The model is not recursive"
A residual covariance between outcomes (m1 ~~ m2)"cannot have a residual covariance (rule 9)"
A label shared by two rows"is used on more than one parameter"
A fixed coefficient (0.3*x, 0*x)"has a fixed coefficient (rule 9)"
A bound (lower(0)*x)"has a bound (rule 9"
==, < or > naming a coefficient label"names the coefficient label"
A fixed, shared or constrained intercept"(rule 9, intercept clause"
meanstructure = FALSE with a product"meanstructure = FALSE, but the model has a product term"
A column m:x in data that is not x * m"is not the product of"
A non-numeric factor"needs numeric variables"
information = "expected", endogenous factor"with a product of an endogenous variable"
anova() or mbco_sem() on such a fit"is not available for ... a model with a product term"
Another product on the treatment or mediator, in extract_mediation()"does not support the product"

Rules 8 and 9 are checked on the parsed table, so they need no data. Rule 8 rejects a regressor built from the outcome (it is correlated with the equation's error); rule 9 names what is not yet supported with products, and the same model works without the product. The covariance that completion would add between two pure outcomes is fixed at 0 in a product model, with one note. Products of observed variables only: a product with a latent variable, x:x and three-way products are not supported.

The global chi-square is not valid when a factor of a product is itself a regression target (the model treats the product as exogenous although it is a function of that variable) or when the exogenous (co)variance block is restricted. glance() then reports chi-square, df and p-value as NA with a note, anova() and mbco_sem() refuse, and expected information is refused for an endogenous product; logLik(), AIC and BIC stay defined. A product of exogenous variables with the block free keeps the ordinary test.

medfit extensions

  • Comma shorthand (medfit extension). A comma-separated left side expands to one statement per name: y1, y2 ~ x means y1 ~ x and y2 ~ x. Commas on the right side are not supported; use +. lavaan reads y1, y2 ~ x differently: it silently keeps only y2. A model copied between the two packages can therefore change meaning without an error.

  • CONSTRAINT(...) (medfit extension). A constraint line may be written CONSTRAINT(a == b), equivalent to the bare a == b. The keyword is case-sensitive and starts the statement, one pair of parentheses encloses the whole constraint, it holds exactly one comparison, and no text follows the closing parenthesis.

Expressions

Both sides of a constraint and the right side of a definition are arithmetic expressions in the labels, with + - * / ^, parentheses, finite numbers, and the functions exp, log, log10, sqrt, abs, min, max, sin, cos, tan, pnorm and qnorm. Anything else is rejected with the construct named.

See also

fit_sem(), SEMFit

Examples

# \donttest{
# Labeled paths and a defined parameter
fit_sem(
  "mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment\nab := a*b",
  data = mediation_demo
)@defined
#>   name expr       est         se
#> 1   ab  a*b 0.3253207 0.08016376

# Comma shorthand: one left-hand side per name
coef(fit_sem(
  "mediator1, mediator2 ~ treatment\noutcome ~ mediator1 + mediator2 + treatment",
  data = mediation_demo
))[1:3]
#> mediator1~treatment mediator2~treatment   outcome~mediator1 
#>           0.4559961           0.2879984           0.5202186 

# An equality constraint, written with the CONSTRAINT() keyword
coef(fit_sem(
  "mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + treatment\nCONSTRAINT(a == b)",
  data = mediation_demo
))[c("a", "b")]
#>         a         b 
#> 0.6673103 0.6673103 
# }
